text: The story uses the phrase "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never a name, keeps the build-dependency row empty and the contract-dependency row as one entry exactly as the Work Package fixes them, and reads the catalog through its contract only.
why: No source names the per-service login, and the Work Package fixes the dependency rows although the pattern set names DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19; the rows are copied rather than edited, and the gap is recorded.
read: Context pack P5 service facts and ownership rows; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 and T3.3; Work Package B2-P5-004; Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.5 DP-01 and DP-11, R9
confirm: RWB-PLT-DB fixes the login names, and the plan confirms or corrects the dependency rows of this slice
impact: No build blocker: the service builds and tests against the contract fake; a published login or an added row changes section 3 and section 12.7 only.

text: The catalog answer is assumed to carry a version identifier, its state, its Legal approval and its merge field list for the requested date, and that identifier is the value written to document.template_id; where no resolved current-version operation exists, the client asks the operation of RWB-P6-E1046-CON and the fake answers the resolved version.
why: The legacy TemplateCatalog.current call returns exactly that answer, and the P6 baseline fixes the rule and the resources but exposes no operation that applies the rule to a date.
read: Legacy story RWB-E1-046 sections 4 and 12; RWB-P6-E1046-CON sections 7 AC3, 11, 12.1 and 12.8; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.3
confirm: RWB-P6-E1046-APP publishes the resolved current-version read and the identifier property before the wave-1 contract tests
impact: No build blocker: the binding is proved against the fake; a different property name changes the client and the fake, not the behaviour.

text: The request field names of GenerateRequest and RegenerateRequest, the reason field, the error body of a refused document, the index ix_document_template and the Flyway step V1046_1__document_template_binding.sql are kept as placeholders until the generation contract publishes them, and no column is added because every column the binding writes already exists in TSD P5 T3.1.
why: The TSD names the two request classes and the reason requirement without their fields, and the run cannot invent contract names; the database columns are already defined, so the migration adds an index only.
read: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.0, T3.1 and T-A.2 (API-P5-006, API-P5-016, API-P5-017); context pack P5 naming rules
confirm: RWB-P5-E2026-CON names the request and reason fields of the two operations
impact: A published name changes one request class and the migration file name; the behaviour and the criteria are unchanged.

text: The P5 feature flag is named rwb.document.template-binding; with the flag off a generation refuses with 503 and the feature-off error of the service template and no document is stamped.
why: The legacy flag rwb.comms.template-catalog belongs to the catalog and the P6 slice, and no source names a P5 flag for the binding; a flag of this service is needed to keep the step releasable on its own.
read: Legacy story RWB-E1-046 section 13 feature flag; RWB-P6-E1046-CON section 13; Template and Rules v1 R4 naming rules and R5.5 DP-19
confirm: RWB-PLT-E1047-CON registers the flag name with its removal date
impact: A renamed flag changes one configuration row and section 13; the behaviour is unchanged.

text: This slice owns no legacy acceptance criterion: legacy AC1 to AC8 and the nine legacy test cases stay with RWB-P6-E1046-APP, and the P5 file lists the nine test cases with the part this service answers named in the Covers column.
why: The split plan gives the P6 story the eight criteria and this slice none, while the Work Package lists all nine test cases for the slice; both facts are kept and stated rather than reconciled by dropping one.
read: Split plan entries RWB-P5-E1046-APP and RWB-P6-E1046-APP; RWB-P6-E1046-CON section 7 closing note; Work Package B2-P5-004 story line
confirm: The traceability owner accepts one owning story per legacy criterion with test-case-bearing secondary slices
impact: Documentation only: no build or test depends on which file owns the criterion.
